steps.prompt: Read both aloud. Which one can you hear?
steps.a: The storm was loud and the rain came down hard on the house.
steps.b:
Crash! The thunder cracked.
Rain rattled the roof, racing, rushing,
drip, drip, drip
on the windowsill.
steps.reveal: The second one uses sound devices: crash, cracked and drip sound like their meaning, and rain rattled the roof, racing, rushing repeats the “r” sound. You don't just read it, you hear it.

cards.title: Four sound devices
cards.body: Alliteration: words close together start with the same sound (silver snakes slither). Onomatopoeia: words that sound like their meaning (sizzle, crash). Rhyme: words that end with the same sound (night, light). Repetition: a word or line that comes back.

cards.title: Sound and mood
cards.body: Sounds carry feeling. Soft sounds (sh, m, l, w) feel calm: “hush, the whispering willows”. Hard sounds (k, t, b, p) feel sharp or loud: “crack, the ticking clock, the banging door”. Choose sounds that match your mood.

cards.title: Forced or natural?
cards.telling:
I saw a cat upon a mat,
it wore a hat and that was that.
cards.showing:
The cat stretched long across the warm mat,
soft as a held breath.
cards.note: Rhyme is optional. If a rhyme forces a silly word, choose another sound device instead.

cards.title: Hear the sounds
cards.prompt: Tap the two words that sound like what they mean.
cards.text: The bacon sizzled in the pan while the old fridge hummed.
